feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence from iteration 1 (entityR2A, 26.64): line_loss_events is 0 on all tracks with the +/-0.05 m spread and 16 mm footprint, and every run still ends off_track with max_error about 0.06 m and progress 0.035 to 0.11. Steering oscillation held near 0.07. So the remaining problem is body response, not sensing. What I had to compensate for: narrowing wheel_track and lowering mass raises turn authority, so I kept kp at 2.0 rather than increasing it, and raised kd from 0.05 to 0.10 to damp the lighter body. Keep ki at 0 and the spread at +/-0.05 m. Next race: if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.1 while max_error stays near 0.06 m, the inertia change is probably too aggressive; revert wheel_track to 0.12 m and keep the lighter body to isolate the effect. If max_error improves but the robot still goes off track, try wheel_track 0.09 m for more turn authority. If line_loss_events goes above 0, the narrower track has moved the sensors relative to the line, so widen the spread to +/-0.065 m.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.1 with max_error still near 0.06 m (iteration 1 showed oscillation 0.07 and max_error 0.06 m), revert wheel_track to 0.12 m and keep the lighter body to isolate the inertia effect.
If max_error falls but runs still go off track (iteration 1 max_error 0.06 m), try wheel_track 0.09 m to add turn authority, keeping mass 0.5 kg.

If line_loss_events rises above 0 (zero in iteration 1), widen sensor x to +/-0.065 m (-0.065, -0.0325, 0, 0.0325, 0.065) with sensor_size 0.016, since the narrower track shifts where the line falls under the sensors.
